problem: Zero-shot VLM navigators are geometrically naive: they cannot reason about 3D layout across views, and prior methods (MapNav, AO-Planner) make them predict raw actions or plan from 2D affordances, entangling semantic reasoning with execution and causing collisions and progress forgetting on long instructions.
motivation: VLMs are strong at semantics and 2D vision but weak at 3D spatial reasoning and translating plans into physical actions, which makes zero-shot VLN-CE unreliable. The paper converts 3D geometry into a 2D form VLMs can read, and hands low-level control to a classical planner.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical (geometric, semantic, decision) 3D map, rasterize it into a BEV image with numbered waypoints as visual prompts so a VLM only selects among geometrically valid waypoints, while A* executes movement and subtask decomposition tracks progress.
insight: Each map layer adds success rate cumulatively (46.0 without BEV, 47.3, 49.2, 51.0 with all three on a 300-episode subset). Removing structured CoT is the most damaging ablation (SR 51.0 to 34.0), followed by subtask decomposition (42.1) and plan-control separation (44.3). Even without the BEV map, HSGM with GPT-5 gets 46.0 SR versus 32.3 for AO-Planner re-run on GPT-5, so the gain comes mainly from the decoupled, 3D-geometry-grounded waypoint framework rather than the stronger backbone.
method: Geometric Map: back-projects RGB-D and pose into a point cloud (following InstructNav), takes points above the ground as obstacles and the rest as navigable area, and adds stairs detected by surface normals and tilted-plane filtering.
Semantic Map: YOLO-E instance segmentation is back-projected to 3D and instances are merged across frames by 3D IoU and label; instances with few points are dropped.

Decision Map: a global waypoint graph (voxel-downsampled navigable points, cylinder collision check, edges of at most 1.0 m and height difference at most 0.3 m) for A*, plus local waypoints in the current view filtered by distance (0.3-3.0 m), obstacle clearance, semantics and reachability.

BEV rasterization and visual prompts: a multi-channel top-down map (obstacles, navigable area, object markers, agent, trajectory, completed-subtask points) plus numbered local waypoints projected onto both the BEV and the front view.

Subtask management: the LLM/VLM splits the instruction into ordered subtasks (each with a verifiable end state and at most 3 motion directives), tracked as pending/in_progress/done, with double STOP confirmation on the last subtask and automatic backtracking to the start when a step limit is exceeded.

Decoupled planning and control: the VLM produces structured CoT (Movement, Observation, Thought, Plan, Action) and picks a waypoint or a 90°/180° turn or STOP; A* on the global graph converts the choice to ROTATE/FORWARD actions.
Multi-floor support: a per-floor map with floor switching by platform detection (RANSAC) and height change, and stairs exempted from obstacle constraints.

setting.backbone: GPT-5 (frozen API) as VLM planner and instruction decomposer; YOLO-E for segmentation
setting.observation: multi-view (front/left/right) RGB-D plus pose, 135° HFOV, 35° downward pitch
setting.action_space: VLM picks among numbered local waypoints or turns (LEFT 90°, RIGHT 90°, TURN AROUND 180°) or STOP; A* converts waypoints into ROTATE/FORWARD low-level actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D for R2R-CE/RxR-CE, HM3D for ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: none (uses depth and pose from the simulator sensors)

results: HSGM reaches SR 47.9 / SPL 32.8 on R2R-CE val-unseen and SR 41.8 / nDTW 54.9 on RxR-CE, beating the best zero-shot baselines (DreamNav 32.8 SR on R2R-CE, AO-Planner 22.4 SR on RxR-CE) and also supervised MapNav (39.7 / 32.6) and NaVid (37.4 / 23.8). On HM3D ObjectNav it gets 73.6 SR, second among zero-shot methods to ApexNav (76.2).
limitations: Depends on GPT-5 API calls that are slow (23.8 s per decision step, 341 s per episode); GPT-4o drops SR to 41.3 on the ablation subset.
The VLM still fails at sequential counting across views and at judging its own position against constraints like 'end of the hallway'.
Relies on simulator RGB-D and pose and a fixed pipeline of hand-tuned thresholds; RxR-CE is evaluated on only 500 English episodes and there is no real-robot test.
